text:
alex: Customer report — their service started getting parse errors this morning when using JSON mode strict. They call our text endpoint with response_format=json&mode=strict and sometimes receive a 200 with an HTML billing page. Their app treats 200+HTML as valid JSON and then crashes on parse.

alex: Quick repro I have (sanitized):
```
curl -v -X POST \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?response_format=json&json_mode=strict\" \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \\
  -H \"Accept: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"hello\"}'
```

alex: Response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 3245
X-Request-Id: r-abc123
```

alex: Body starts with `<html>...Payment required...` so parser errors out. Customer says it happens intermittently (maybe during billing checks).

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026 created and linked to this thread.

maria: Thanks @alex. Can you paste the full raw response body (or first 1k chars) and confirm whether the request had any retries that returned non-200 codes previously? Also which plan/customer id?

alex: Pasted first 600 chars in ticket. No earlier non-200 codes in their logs — just sudden 200+HTML responses starting ~08:20 UTC. They mentioned a billing update earlier in their account but didn't see alerts.

liam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) upstream billing/service is returning an HTML error page and our edge is passing through 200 with HTML (bad). 2) Negotiation fallthrough: client requests JSON but our edge prefers upstream content-type and doesn't enforce response_format in strict mode when a different internal service returns HTML.

emily: Workaround for the customer while we investigate: set Accept header to `application/json; profile=redwood.v1+json` and include header `X-Redwood-Enforce: response_format` to force JSON negotiation server-side. Also try adding `&response_fallback=auto` (safe option) so the client gets a structured error object instead of raw HTML. Tell them to avoid strict parsing until we confirm.

maria: Can engineering check edge logs for X-Request-Id r-abc123 and see which upstream returned the HTML? If it's billing-service, escalate to billing. If it's our proxy accidentally mapping 402 -> 200, that's high-sev.

oncall: I'm on it, pulling logs now. Can someone confirm the exact query params used? We need the `json_mode` vs `mode` mismatch check (some clients use `json_mode=strict`, others `mode=strict`).

alex: They used `json_mode=strict` in their code. Repro curl above uses `json_mode=strict` too.

oncall: Found matching request: r-abc123 forwarded to billing-check-v2 which returned 402 HTML and our edge returned upstream body but coalesced status to 200 because of an internal header rewrite bug. Root cause looks like `preserve_status=false` set in a recent deploy to reduce 5xx churn. Rolling back that flag for the edge routing.

liam: Good catch. Priority: rollback + patch to enforce content-type matching when `response_format=json` or `json_mode=strict` is set. We should return a 4xx/5xx and a JSON error object, not HTML.

emily: Practical customer note to paste in ticket: \"We're aware of intermittent HTML error pages leaking through in strict JSON mode. Temporary workaround: add Accept: application/json; profile=redwood.v1+json and set response_fallback=auto. We're rolling back the edge flag and will deploy a fix to enforce response format semantics.\" :thumbsup:

maria: Also flagging billing team to review why billing-check-v2 returned HTML instead of a JSON error. Billing, FYI: request id r-abc123 around 08:20 UTC.

support-bot: Pushed status update to ticket #INC-2026: Rollback started, customer workaround suggested.

alex: Customer confirmed workaround works for one retry. They'll hold on rolling to prod until we confirm fix.

oncall: Rollback finished. Edge now returns 402 with JSON body when upstream returns error. Monitoring for 10m.

maria: Thanks all — assign follow-up to eng-runtime to add a unit/integration test that simulates upstream HTML error in strict JSON mode. Also add a runbook entry for Accept header enforcement.

liam: I'll open a PR for the content-type enforcement and add the test. ETA end of day.

emily: Great. Closing the Slack thread once ticket gets updated and customer notified. :white_check_mark:
